title: Hidden Windows launcher makes native startup failures look like an unexplained flash-exit
summary: Quick-Automatic-Hardsub-Encoder's Windows startup regression was traced to a malformed PowerShell return/if construct in windows/native-backend.ps1: `return if($Name -eq 'ffmpeg'){$toolchain.Ffmpeg}else{$toolchain.Ffprobe}` inside Find-NativeTool. The bridge dot-sources this file at startup, so the syntax/runtime parse failure aborts Native Bridge before the browser opens. The normal launcher starts PowerShell hidden and exits immediately, making the actual error appear as an unexplained flash-exit. Fix the conditional with explicit branch returns and retain a visible/durable startup-failure path.

evidence.user_report: Windows version flashes and exits immediately on the user's machine.
evidence.launcher: windows/start_windows.bat uses start powershell.exe ... -WindowStyle Hidden -File native-bridge.ps1, then exit /b 0.
evidence.debug_path: windows/start_windows_debug.bat runs the same bridge visibly and pauses on non-zero exit.
evidence.code_observation: native-bridge.ps1 handles missing FFmpeg with a MessageBox, but other top-level startup exceptions are not wrapped in a visible failure path.
evidence.root_cause: windows/native-backend.ps1 Find-NativeTool contains `return if(...)`; replace with explicit `if (...) { return ... }` followed by fallback return.
evidence.failure_path: native-bridge.ps1 dot-sources native-backend.ps1 before creating the listener/browser launch, so a parse failure aborts the bridge during startup.
